text:
🚨 After hours of research, I finally figured out why bitcoin is still not going up.

Everyone’s asking me why BTC can’t get a real breakout while stocks rip and gold flies…

So I dug for hours.

The answer is hiding in options flow, and these charts tell the whole story.

Let me explain what’s actually happening:

Long-time Bitcoin holders are quietly selling into strength.

Not just spot selling, but selling upside through options.

That constant supply caps rallies and kills momentum before it ever snowballs.

At the same time, ETF buyers are doing the opposite.

IBIT traders are paying up for upside.

They want calls and they’re betting on higher prices months out.

So you end up with a split market.

Native BTC markets are suppressing volatility while ETF markets are bidding for it.

That mismatch matters more than price itself.

When volatility gets crushed, BTC chops sideways.

No squeeze or melt-up, just frustration.

That’s exactly what we’ve seen as implied vol slid from the low 60s back into the mid 40s.

The charts show it clearly:

IBIT has upside demand but BTC doesn’t.

Until that flips, Bitcoin stays a trader’s market, not a trend market.

The next real move doesn’t start with price, it starts when volatility finally comes back.

On another note, I called the exact bottom at $16k and the top at $126k and i’ll do it again. When it’s a good time to buy, i’ll announce it here publicly.

Many people will wish they followed me sooner.
